This neonatal mass is comparatively low among Calidris species, suggesting a trade-off between early hatchling size and the rapid growth necessary to fledge before the brief Arctic summer ends.

Adults of this species exhibit pronounced sexual dimorphism in body mass, with females reaching an ultimate wet weight of 45.8 grams [Wwi = 45.8 grams] during the breeding season, while males attain a slightly lower asymptotic mass of 43 grams [Wwi = 43 grams]. This early mass is markedly lower than the adult female asymptotic mass of 45.8 grams [Wwi = 45.8 grams], underscoring the dramatic growth trajectory required during the short Arctic summer.
